expectations.text: Writes the messaging angle as a conversational sentence a customer could plausibly say out loud, not a tagline or a feature list
expectations.evidence: §3 Message states the messaging angle as: *"I don't want to pop a pill that makes me groggy the next day just to fall asleep."* — a first-person, spoken-sounding complaint, not a slogan or feature list. It is explicitly self-checked against the say-it-out-loud test ('Test: a customer could plausibly say this out loud — passes.'), and the adjacent Value prop field keeps the product-benefit phrasing separate from the angle, so the angle field is not contaminated by feature language. The completion test ('wait, melatonin might be the problem, not the fix...') is likewise written in customer voice
